title: The three-dimensional Ball–Evans approximation problem

manuscripts.title: Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for 1<=p<=2
Strong diffeomorphic approximation in three dimensions for p>2

main_statement.latex: Let $\Omega,\Lambda\subset\R^3$ be nonempty bounded connected open sets, let $1\le p\le2$ [resp. $2<p<\infty$], and let $f:\Omega\to\Lambda$ be a homeomorphism in $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\R^3)$. There exist $C^\infty$ diffeomorphisms $f_j:\Omega\to\Lambda$, each belonging to $W^{1,p}(\Omega;\R^3)$, such that $\int_\Omega( |f_j-f|^p+|Df_j-Df|^p)\,dx\to0$.
main_statement.paraphrase: In dimension three, every Sobolev homeomorphism between bounded domains, for any finite p>=1, is a strong W^{1,p} limit of smooth diffeomorphisms onto the same target. No boundary regularity, inverse regularity, or Jacobian sign is assumed. This settles the 3D Ball-Evans approximation problem affirmatively (it fails in dimension >=4 for p<[n/2], by Campbell-Hencl-Tengvall).
main_statement.note_for_comparator: No Lean formalization. The family splits by exponent: M1 (1<=p<=2) by budgets of measured traces; M2 (p>2) by an exact carrier, a convex quantizer onto a 2-complex and guard-pinned wall realization.

flags.full_only_with_prior_results_detail: Each manuscript covers half the exponent range (1<=p<=2; 2<p<infty); the family is complete only by combining the two OpenAI manuscripts, which are logically independent of each other ('No theorem from that range is used here', M2:01-introduction.tex:57-58). flags.adds_corollaries_detail: By-product: strong W^{1,p} approximation by locally finite PL homeomorphisms (Prop sm:bilip-pl composed with the main constructions), the PL version of Ball's question. No inverse (bi-Sobolev) convergence claimed.

evidence.quote: We resolve the three-dimensional Ball--Evans approximation problem for $1\le p\le2$.

B.note: Ball-Evans is a question (Ball 2001, attributing to Evans); 3D was open per Hencl 2025 survey. Affirmative resolution for all finite p (n=3), fixed target, no boundary regularity.

proof_architecture.claim: Smoothing theorem: locally bi-Lipschitz W^{1,p} homeomorphism -> PL (finite libraries before resolution) -> diffeomorphism onto the same target (degree argument).
Select compact jet sets by rank (tail small); fix l, sharp tolerances, then mesh.

Topological budget transfer: clean crossings of measured source traces (edges; faces if p=2) with random target dual strata; regularize; softmax-squeeze target so image length/area <= tie budget; E[budget] <= C trace integral.
Rank 3: radial blocks with identity germs (star replacement) recover jets; p=2 needs reverse rays (inverse BV) and angular attenuation.

Rank 1/2: kernel compression to line/plane sections; near-sharp budgets on anisotropic grids; length identity (rank 1), sharp disk estimate (rank 2, p=2), planar radial blocks + collapse (rank 2, p<2).
Complete uncontrolled cells by collapse/disk estimates; sum; smooth.
Regular points (p>2); flatten deficient-rank image onto plates via decomposability bundle; protected double wells.
Exact carrier F_b by immersed-skeleton cutoffs (universal energy constant, ball fibres), regular affine implants, exceptional marked cubes (2<p<3).
Convex quantizer T onto a 2-complex with blocks in exact regions; polar labels (t,s) on faces; graph exterior with annulus/disk walls.

Pull back sampled walls, normalize (Haken), build pre-stacks with slope majorant G (sharp on calibrated islands via snapping/broadening); fix capacities; choose guards; route walls; guard barrier pins labels; realize homeomorphism h.

Final map P_0 T h: derivative from labels only; sharp energy + pinned mean => strong gradient convergence (uniform convexity); strictify; compress marked cubes; smooth; full-rank cube correction; smooth.

eureka_candidates.item: M2-31 + M2-34 + M2-36 + M2-37 (guard-pinned wall realization; energy through labels only)
eureka_candidates.for: Nothing in L or the goal resembles realizing the two polar label coordinates (t,s) of a 2-complex-valued map as level walls of a homeomorphism, routing them with conserved parameter length, and pinning the realized labels by reference fibre paths ('guards') through a capacity barrier that diverges like h^{2-p}. It makes the final energy depend only on scalar parameter slopes, never on Dh, which is what lets the p>2 proof survive without a quantitative 3D extension theorem.
eureka_candidates.against: Ingredients are classical: oscillation of W^{1,p} functions on 2-spheres for p>2 (Morrey/Gehring), intersection numbers via H_2=0, Haken regular exchange. Planar precedents (IKO 2011 coordinatewise p-harmonic replacement; Ntalampekos 2019 monotone level sets) represent maps via scalar coordinates. A judge could call it a combination of known parts.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour: IKO 2011 coordinatewise p-harmonic replacement (planar); Ntalampekos arXiv:1911.06619 (level sets of planar monotone Sobolev functions); Gehring oscillation lemma. None realize labels topologically in 3D or use guards.
eureka_candidates.lit_check: WebSearch 2026-10-09 (level sets/pinning/oscillation on spheres + Sobolev homeomorphism approximation): no match.

eureka_candidates.item: M2-08 + M2-09 immersed cubical skeleton cutoff
eureka_candidates.for: A universal-constant energy bound for cutting a near-identity Sobolev homeomorphism off to the identity, obtained by lifting through an immersion of a Whitney-layered 2-skeleton at a common scale s ((l/s)^3 volume factor vs (s/l)^2 overlap) and collapsing uncontrolled hole fillings to points. Replaces the missing 3D quantitative extension theorem; used for every exact implant.
eureka_candidates.against: Lifting a near-identity homeomorphism through an immersion is Kirby's torus trick (1969) / Edwards-Kirby (cited for M1-08); the novelty is quantitative scaling.
eureka_candidates.nearest_neighbour: Kirby 1969 torus trick; Edwards-Kirby 1971. Not cited for this lemma.
eureka_candidates.lit_check: WebSearch 2026-10-09 'Kirby torus trick immersion lift ... Sobolev energy Whitney': only topological sources.

eureka_candidates.item: M1-27 + M1-28 + M1-29 tie budget and variable softmax simplex squeeze
eureka_candidates.for: Converts counts of crossings with barycentric-tie dual strata of a random target triangulation into actual image lengths/areas of a homeomorphism, via a face-compatible, injective softmax concentration. Gives the low-exponent energy bounds without any derivative bound on the topological replacement.
eureka_candidates.against: Dual-cell crossing counts are the Federer-Fleming deformation mechanism, and the paper cites White 1999 Prop 2.2 as precedent.
eureka_candidates.lit_check: WebSearch 2026-10-09: no homeomorphism-valued realization of FF deformation found.

eureka_candidates.item: M2-19 + M2-17 convex product quantizer with Poisson contact exclusion
eureka_candidates.for: Reduces the 3D target to a polyhedral 2-complex (orthogonal product fibres) whose 3D blocks lie in exact regions; makes 2 scalar labels carry the deficient-rank gradient.
eureka_candidates.against: Moreau proximal maps and power diagrams (both cited) give the construction; contact exclusion by negative Laplacian is elementary.

eureka_candidates.item: M1-14 finite PL libraries before resolution
eureka_candidates.for: Fixes derivative bounds of qualitative PL replacements before shrinking the exceptional set, breaking a circularity.
eureka_candidates.against: Paper names Vaisala 1977 (Carleson's method) as precedent.

correctness_audit.verdict: No gap found in the parts checked, but the family is ~15,000 lines of dense, unreviewed argument with no formalization and no reasoning trace. It is an extraordinary claim (open problem per Hencl 2025) and needs expert review.
checked: M2-09 energy summation: per depth lambda, lift energy <= (lambda/s)^3 x overlap count (s/lambda)^2 => geometric series; requires |Di||Di^{-1}| bounded (holds by (hp:immersion-bounds)). Correct.
M2-12: cost |Db|^p R^3/det Db vs int_{V_b}|DF|^p >= c|Db|^p|V_b|, |V_b| ~ R^3/det Db: condition number cancels. Correct.
M2-21: (T_eta(y1)-T_eta(y2)).(q1-q2) >= (1-||eta||-M Lip eta)|q1-q2|^2 using monotonicity of T; injective. Correct.
M2-34 barrier arithmetic: c_delta <= C R^{1-2/p}||G||_{L^p(Sigma_R)} => int_{Sigma_R}G^p >= c R^{2-p}; integrate R in [h,2h], times c a/h balls => c a h^{2-p} -> infinity iff p>2. Correct.
M2-49 uniform convexity inequality for p>2 and the cancellation r||V^{-1}|| <= C|Df|. Plausible.
M1-17 sharp disk: total energy 2 Area <= 2+o(1), X and Y each >= 1-o(1) by segment Cauchy-Schwarz => remaining components vanish and DX,DY -> rows of I. Correct.
M1-14: second-round library models agree with L on good cubes because the model must realize older protected data (including the cube's own first-round core). Consistent.
Split at p=2 is coherent: face energy can be bounded by image area only when p<=2.
concerns: Scale and opacity: dozens of 'order of choices' dependencies (Remark ha:scale-order; M1:04:1154-1190). Circularity is explicitly addressed but cannot be checked line by line here.

Heavy reliance on qualitative topology in specific relative forms (Hamilton relative approximation for noncompact manifolds with fine tolerance; Edwards-Kirby uniform over finite configuration lists; relative Smale-Hirsch with target ball). These are standard but the exact relative versions used are asserted, not quoted.

M2 Theorem wl:realization is explicitly conditional; its hypotheses are discharged in Secs 8-9 (Prop ha:initial-walls). The ball/disk recognition in the proof (patch-balls, no leftover component) is intricate.
M1 Lemma lt:squeeze: injectivity proof with variable exponent a(lambda) (monotonicity in trial D) is terse.
Mutual companion citations: both manuscripts claim independence; the smoothing appendix is duplicated with small edits (diffed).
No numerical claims or computer search to audit; no Lean.
consistency_checks: Catalog summary (1<=p<infty, bounded domains, fixed target) matches the two headline theorems.
Both papers share identical conventions and Lemma pre:local-tolerances text.

extraction_friction: Two manuscripts, logically independent, sharing a duplicated smoothing section (M1 Sec 2 = M2 Appendix A, minor wording diffs). Items extracted once (M1-07..14) with M2-50 as duplicate.

Very few \emph definitions; most load-bearing objects (carrier, guards, quantizer, walls, budgets) are defined inside proofs or in 'Definition' environments with prose names. A naive extractor would miss the softmax squeeze formula (inside a lemma) and the guard notion (Definition wl:guards plus prose in the intro).
Many labels are double (\label{lt:star-replacement}\label{lt:star}); main theorem labels collide across manuscripts (main:theorem in both).
Proof architecture is governed by an 'order of choices' rather than a lemma DAG; dependencies on later sections (Theorem wl:realization is conditional on Secs 8-9).

Precedent cues: 'classical precursor in Morrey', 'appear in Vaisala's implementation of Carleson's method', 'Counting intersections with complementary cells is also central to polyhedral deformation; see White', 'graph-parametrized form of Alberti--Marchese's Lemma 7.5', 'related to regular exchange in normal-surface theory', 'following Haken's normalization method', 'planar construction of Hencl--Pratelli'.
No Lean; load-bearing shares estimated from prose architecture only.
